processing_steps.atmosphere: toluene (process control reagent, to avoid oxidation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Elemental Fe, Ni, Mn, Al, Si and C powder (99.2% pure) taken in the proportion Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 and milled in a planetary ball mill (Model no. PM 400/2, Retsch) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; WC vials and WC balls; toluene added as process control reagent to avoid oxidation. Milling was stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating. This 20 h state is a snapshot of a continuous milling campaign up to 35 h (2–3 g powder sampled after every 5 h of milling).

structures.overall_structure: Mechanically alloyed (milled) powder after 20 h: an intermediate milling state in which alloying is in progress. The intense Ni and Mn elemental peaks are no longer evident in the XRD pattern, whereas all low-intensity elemental peaks had already vanished after 5 h and Al largely dissolved by 15 h. A fully alloyed solid solution (BCC + γ-brass type) is only reported after 25 h, so at 20 h the powder is not yet a single-phase solid solution. Powder particles are markedly refined relative to earlier milling times (bulky/coarse at 10 h).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EMPYREAN, PANALYTICAL with Co-Kα source (operating voltage 40 kV; operating current 40 mA; scan rate 5°·min−1)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; milled powder after 20 h of milling, part of the XRD series recorded at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 h of milling
characterization_methods.purpose: To study the alloying behavior / phase evolution of the powder as a function of milling time
characterization_methods.key_findings: After 20 h of milling the intense peaks of Ni and Mn are no longer evident in the XRD pattern; low-intensity elemental peaks had vanished after 5 h and Al diminished after 15 h, indicating progressive alloying.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Evo 18 Carl Zeiss SEM (with EDS detector)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Milled powder after 20 h of milling (Fig. 2(b) micrograph, 2 µm scale bar)
characterization_methods.purpose: To examine the size, shape and morphology of the milled powder at different milling times
characterization_methods.key_findings: Particle morphology is finer and more fractured than at 10 h; the average particle size decreases drastically after 20 h of milling.

characterization_methods.technique: Particle-size distribution analysis (image analysis of SEM micrographs)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ImageJ software applied to SEM micrographs
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Particle-size histogram for 20 h milled powder (Fig. 2(g)), x-axis about 1–11 µm
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine the particle size distribution of the milled powder as a function of milling time
characterization_methods.key_findings: Average particle size after 20 h of milling is ~6 ± 2 µm (Gaussian fit).

unmapped_findings: The 20 h milled powder is an intermediate milling state: after 20 h of milling the intense Ni and Mn elemental peaks are no longer evident in the XRD pattern, whereas Al had already largely dissolved by 15 h; a fully alloyed solid solution consisting of BCC (a = 0.286 nm) and γ-brass type (a = 0.872 nm) is only reported after 25 h of milling.
Average powder particle size after 20 h of milling is ~6 ± 2 µm (SEM particle-size histogram, Gaussian fit; particle-size x-range about 1–11 µm).

The 20 h milled powder is the state in which 'the average particle sizes decreased drastically' relative to earlier milling times; the powder progressively becomes more homogeneous with increasing milling time.
